verses.text: As the number of disciples kept growing, the Greek-speaking believers complained against the Hebrew-speaking believers because their widows were being overlooked in the daily food distribution.
The Twelve called all the disciples together and said, “It wouldn’t be right for us to stop teaching God’s word so we can manage the food service.
“So, brothers and sisters, choose seven respected men from among you, full of the Spirit and wisdom. We’ll put them in charge of this work.
“Then we can keep giving ourselves to prayer and to serving through the word.”
This proposal pleased everyone. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit; Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a convert from Antioch.
They brought these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
God’s word continued to spread, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem grew rapidly. A large number of priests also accepted the faith.
Stephen, full of grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.
But some people from the synagogue called the Freedmen—including people from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia—started arguing with Stephen.
They couldn’t stand up to the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
So they secretly persuaded some men to claim, “We heard him speak against Moses and God.”
They stirred up the people, elders, and scribes, then came after Stephen, seized him, and brought him before the council.
They brought in false witnesses, who said, “This man is always speaking against this holy place and the law.
“We heard him say that Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us.”
Everyone sitting in the council stared at Stephen and saw that his face looked like an angel’s.
